evidence.title: [2609.09233] Subagents vs Agent Skills: Executing Reusable Knowledge for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
Subagents vs Agent Skills: Executing Reusable Knowledge for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

name: Subagents vs Agent Skills
summary: arXiv paper comparing running reusable agent skills as subagents against loading skill instructions into the main context.
description: Agent skills are multi-file packages of instructions and scripts that agents usually execute by loading them into their context, which gets brittle as task horizons grow. The paper shows that executing the same skill packages as subagents with clear input-output contracts lowers peak context length and outperforms agent-skill execution on SkillsBench, at the cost of extra coordination tokens.
